h: Lennon, McCartney and the Calder Stones
p: Hunts Cross is in the south of Liverpool, near the airport and a world away from the busy city centre. Hunts Cross station is on the Merseyrail Northern line, so you can reach the shopping centre by train, and the A562 and M62 are close for drivers.

South Liverpool is Beatles country in a big way. In the nearby suburb of Woolton, John Lennon and Paul McCartney first met at the St Peter's Church garden fete in 1957, and Strawberry Field, the children's home that inspired the song, is now open to visitors with an exhibition and gardens. Even if your kids think the Beatles are ancient history, it's a fun detour for the grown-ups.

Calderstones Park, a short drive north, is a big, leafy park that takes its name from the Calder Stones, ancient carved stones that are thousands of years old. There are gardens, play areas and plenty of space for a picnic.

Liverpool John Lennon Airport is right next door, and kids who love planes will enjoy watching them come in low over the area. Further along the river, the old village of Hale is famous for the legend of the Childe of Hale, said to have been a giant, and there's a carved statue in his honour.
With so much to choose from, you could easily spend a whole weekend in this corner of the city without going near the centre.

If the Beatles bug bites, many Beatles fans also make the trip to Mendips, Lennon's childhood home in Woolton, and Forthlin Road, where McCartney grew up in Allerton. Both are run by the National Trust and can only be seen on a booked tour, so plan ahead rather than just turning up at the door.
